title: Take a stance
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which side are you on, and have you thought about it?

A student in the banking industry said they are aggressively looking to streamline efficiencies with AI, especially in customer service. When people call a company they sometimes really want to speak to a human being, because they feel more understood.
The student said we will lose a lot of that: you will see fewer human beings on the phone. What we lose is sympathy, the ability to understand what a customer is feeling.
Jose said it is interesting where these two men draw the line philosophically, because it prompts us as business people and as thinking human beings: are we on one side or the other?

It is something we cannot avoid, he said. We are going to have to take a stance, and the awareness of that decision, and where we stand, is very important. A lot of people won't think about these questions.
A student said: can I keep agreeing to the terms and conditions without reading them? Jose said: yes, and there is a revolutionary impact in what these people are doing.
Some of them say: we have a massive responsibility to humanity. Others say: I'm just going to profit from it and offer the technology, Jose said. He added that he is not trying to make a judgment.
He said to look up these companies and see what they are doing in real life, and to see whether it is consistent with the way the author writes the story.
Where do you draw your line, and what would you do if you had to defend it?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what a customer loses when a machine answers.
Write where you want a human to answer.
Write where you draw your line on technology and why.
Write a company you will look up to see whether it matches its story.
Write how you will tell your team where you stand.

check.q: What did a student say customers sometimes really want?
choices: To speak with a human being

check.q: What did Jose say we are going to have to do?
What did Jose say to do about what an author writes?
choices: Look up the companies and see if it's consistent

recap: Know the cost of automating. Take a stance and defend it.
